base_properties.human_readable: Thinkability-Origin Dating Convention for Electronic Money

omegas.question: This constraint is the became_thinkable reading of kernel electronic_money_emergence; what would change structurally if either sibling reading were instantiated instead?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Generate the first_held and m4_m5_collapse stories and compare computed seats across the three files: relocation of beneficiaries toward institutional operators under first_held; re-seating of monetary_statisticians from payers toward artifact-authors and deflation of the category under m4_m5_collapse.
omegas.impact: If a sibling reading dominates the field, this file's victim set and its gain_flow seat dissolve: under first_held the credit flow moves to institutional bearers; under m4_m5_collapse there is no substantive emergence to allocate credit for, and the convention's extraction registers as artifact-maintenance rather than attribution transfer.
omegas.description: Committer-frame index: this story is one of three readings of the emergence-dating kernel; siblings alter epsilon, beneficiary structure, and victim set.

omegas.question: Which moment counts as 'technically and socially thinkable' — blind-signature publication, earlier cybernetic and fiction speculation, or first working prototype trials — and does the choice move the origin point, and with it the collected credit?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Citation-network and archival dating of when electronic-money possibility entered expert and popular discourse; sensitivity analysis re-running the periodization under each candidate anchor.
omegas.impact: Earlier or broader anchors widen the beneficiary class (fiction writers, theorists, popularizers) and raise measured credit concentration; narrow technical anchors shrink it and pull epsilon toward the threshold reading.
omegas.description: Indeterminacy of the thinkability criterion that fixes this reading's origin point.

omegas.question: Was the decades-long lag between thinkability and statistical registration caused by institutional conservatism (avoidable) or by genuine epistemic difficulty of measuring dematerialized value (necessary)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative study of statistical agencies that registered electronic payment flows early versus late, controlling for data infrastructure; internal review records of aggregate-definition debates.
omegas.impact: If conservatism dominates, the statisticians' target weighting strengthens and the convention's suppressive component rises; if necessity dominates, part of the lag-attributed grievance is misallocated and effective extraction falls.
omegas.description: Whether the celebrated measurement lag was avoidable gatekeeping or hard epistemics.

omegas.question: How many functioning electronic-money deployments originated outside the metropolitan conceptual circuit and therefore never received an assigned thinkable moment?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Systematic inventory of retail e-money and electronic purse launches in non-center economies with launch dates and local documentation, cross-checked against the canon's coverage of each.
omegas.impact: Documented peripheral origination raises the erasure component of effective extraction and would justify moving peripheral_deployment_pioneers from excluded to payer with formal structural declaration.
omegas.description: Extent of off-center origination invisible to diffusion-centered dating.

commentary.narrative_context: The colloquial question 'when did electronic money emerge?' decomposes, under the epsilon-invariance principle, into three structurally distinct constraints corresponding to the three declared readings of kernel electronic_money_emergence; this story instantiates the became_thinkable reading alone. Under this reading, the standing arrangement under contest is the historiographic convention — maintained through journal editing, curriculum committees, and commemorative calendars — that dates electronic money's emergence to the moment its possibility became technically and socially thinkable, with official measurement arriving decades later. Assessed by this reading's own lights, the convention genuinely coordinates: one shared origin enables cumulative scholarship, teachable chronologies, and policy lineage-telling. The same convention also transfers attributional credit and narrative authority away from operational implementers (clearing, card, and funds-transfer engineers) and measurement institutions (monetary statisticians) toward conceptual innovators and their chroniclers — coordination and asymmetric transfer run through one structure, hence the tangled_rope claim. The epsilon referent is this convention as it stands, not any rival dating a sibling would install: the first_held sibling would relocate beneficiaries toward institutional operators and re-date the origin to a datable holding event; the m4_m5_collapse sibling would deflate the category to a statistical artifact and re-seat the statisticians. Those are separate files with their own epsilon values, beneficiaries, and victims; they appear here only as linked constraints. Interval mapping: time unit is approximately one year, t=0 the mid-1990s consolidation of the thinkable frame in monetary-history curricula, t=30 the mid-2020s.
key_agents: digital_cash_conceptualists: primary beneficiary (moderate/mobile) — collects founding credit under thinkability dating
historians_of_technology: secondary beneficiary (moderate/mobile) — harvest the narrative arc
central_bank_narrative_units: tertiary beneficiary (institutional/constrained) — convert the frame into lineage legitimacy
monetary_history_editorial_boards: agenda_setter (institutional/identity_locked) — administers canons, curricula, and commemorative calendars
payment_systems_implementers: primary target (organized/constrained) — operational priority rendered as implementation detail
monetary_statisticians: secondary target (institutional/constrained) — measurement work recast as institutional lag
peripheral_deployment_pioneers: excluded voice (powerless/trapped) — deployments fall outside the arc entirely
economic_methodologists: analytical observer (analytical/analytical) — treats all three periodizations as framings with distributive effects
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness is moderate (0.52 at interval end): the convention's transfer is real but denominated in credit, citation primacy, and narrative authority rather than income, and the transferred amounts are decoupled from the scale of the implementers' and statisticians' actual contributions. Suppression is moderate-low (0.38): rival periodizations remain publishable and no coercion backs the frame; the friction is editorial and curatorial. Theater_ratio (0.34) is deliberately rising across the series — anniversary volumes, commemorative conferences, and retrospective exhibitions increasingly substitute for analytic work on the origin question, a Goodhart-drift signature. Accessibility_collapse is low (0.32): once the convention is understood, rival datings do NOT collapse — threshold histories and measurement-skeptic literatures remain fully accessible, which is characteristic of a construct that must be continuously maintained rather than a limit that enforces itself. Resistance is moderate (0.44): sustained priority disputes, practitioner memoirs, and methodological critique meet the frame continuously. Claim and metrics are independent authored facts: the tangled_rope claim comes from the structure (one periodization simultaneously coordinating and transferring), the metrics from the described operation. Both measurement series share one grid (every five years, t=0..30) so no metric row is backfilled from another's endpoints. Suppression_requirement is intentionally not tracked as a series: the enforcement picture (editorial and curricular gatekeeping) is roughly static across the interval, and the scalar captures it; the traced dynamics are credit concentration and commemoration drift.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The seats should compute differently. From the payer seats — implementers and statisticians — the convention operates as enforced erasure: their priority claims are structurally unheard, and the machinery that maintains the frame is the same machinery that declines their submissions, so their experienced type sits nearer the pure-extraction end. From the beneficiary seats the identical structure operates as an enabling frame that makes their work legible and fundable, computing nearer the pure-coordination end. The agenda-setter seat experiences stewardship: editorial boards do not experience themselves as collecting anything, but as custodians of a canon whose revision would repudiate their institutions' own catalogs — an institutional identity fusion that makes their exit effectively unavailable regardless of intellectual persuasion.
commentary.directionality_logic: Declared beneficiaries (conceptualists, historians, central-bank narrative units) derive low directionality — the convention subsidizes their credit positions, and the conceptualists' mobility keeps them nearest the subsidy end. Declared victims (implementers, statisticians) derive high directionality: they bear the transfer, and their constrained exits (career and institutional ties to the very institutions hosting the canon) trap them nearer the full-target end than their formal power would suggest. One explicit override: peripheral_deployment_pioneers carry no beneficiary/victim declaration because they are formally outside the ledger — the canonical fallback for a powerless agent would land them near symmetric, which misdescribes them. Their actual structural position is near-full target of the erasure flow (their origination dates simply do not count), so the override sets the powerless atom to d=0.82. Scope amplification is modest here: the convention operates globally but verification of any particular attribution dispute is local and archival.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem — the need for one narratable origin after decades of fragmentary deployments made any single deployment-date answer unmanageable — is real and partially live: each new payment wave re-triggers origin questions, which is why the convention persists. But its settlement is disputed, hence founding_problem_status=contested. Because status is contested rather than dead, the status-by-disappearance mismatch flag does not fire: the arrangement is not a zombie maintaining itself after its problem expired; the problem is alive but its solution is contested. The classification guards against both mislabelings: calling the convention a pure rope would erase the credit-transfer asymmetry that implementers and statisticians demonstrably bear; calling it a snare would erase the genuine coordination without which cumulative monetary historiography loses its anchor. The rising theater_ratio is watched separately as a degradation signal — if commemoration continues substituting for analysis, the convention drifts toward inertial maintenance, and a future re-authoring at higher theater with the same transfer structure would warrant revisiting this claim.
commentary.kernel_context: Kernel: electronic_money_emergence — the question of when electronic money began. This file instantiates the became_thinkable_reading: emergence as a gradual conceptual-social diffusion completed before any institutional measurement registered it. Sibling readings, each a separate constraint file: first_held_reading (emergence is a datable institutional threshold — the first bearer holding dematerialized currency) and m4_m5_collapse_reading (the category itself was created retroactively by statistical practice, making 'emergence' a measurement artifact). The disagreement is located in the ontological status of the emergence event — diffuse process, datable threshold, or measurement artifact — and because each reading fixes a different origin ontology, each authors a different epsilon and a different beneficiary/victim structure. This reading holds the process ontology and therefore authors moderate epsilon with conceptualists as the credit-receiving seat.

network.dual_formulation_note: Constraint-family decomposition record: one colloquial label ('the emergence of electronic money') covered three structurally distinct claims with different epsilon values and different party structures — became_thinkable_reading (this file: process ontology, epsilon ~0.52, credit transfer to conceptualists), first_held_reading (threshold ontology; beneficiaries would relocate to institutional operators), and m4_m5_collapse_reading (artifact ontology; epsilon collapses toward artifact-maintenance and the statisticians re-seat from payers to the practice that constituted the category). Authored as three files per the epsilon-invariance rule and linked pairwise. Upstream/downstream: this reading is the currently dominant frame and thereby conditions the operating environment (venue access, commemorative calendars, curricular slots) within which the sibling readings compete, which is why the edges run from this file to the siblings.

stakeholders.name: digital_cash_conceptualists
stakeholders.situation: Cryptographers, protocol designers, and technology writers who articulated electronic-money schemes before deployment — blind-signature cash designs, stored-value proposals, cryptographic payment essays. The dating convention locates the origin of electronic money in their moment, so anniversaries, citation primacy, patent-lineage claims, and invited-historian roles flow to them. Exit is easy in the ordinary sense: they work across universities, firms, and standards bodies, and their standing survives whichever periodization wins.

stakeholders.name: historians_of_technology
stakeholders.situation: Scholars who organize the archive of payments history around a conceptual-origin arc. The frame supplies conference themes, monograph structures, and a clean narrative of imagination preceding realization. Switching frames would strand part of their published corpus, so they defend the anchor while acknowledging rival datings in footnotes.

stakeholders.name: central_bank_narrative_units
stakeholders.situation: Communications and history teams at central banks and international bodies that tell long-lineage stories to legitimize current initiatives such as retail digital currency and real-time payment rails. The thinkable frame gives them depth: today's project becomes the latest chapter of a decades-old idea. Their movement is bounded by institutional messaging discipline — a public re-dating would contradict their own prior publications.

stakeholders.name: monetary_history_editorial_boards
stakeholders.situation: Journal editors, handbook series editors, and curriculum committee members who decide which periodization enters textbooks, handbooks, and anniversary volumes. They administer the chronology rather than merely drawing on it. Their institutions have become identified with the established account — re-anchoring would repudiate catalogs, funded series, and prior editorial commitments — so revision is practically unavailable to them even where individually attractive.

stakeholders.name: payment_systems_implementers
stakeholders.situation: Engineers and operations staff who built and ran the working electronic payment systems — interbank funds transfer, card authorization networks, automated clearing, early stored-value rollouts. Under the thinkable frame their systems appear after the 'real' origin, as implementation following the conceptual event, and their project records rarely reach the origin story. They retain professional channels and could publish counter-histories, but career ties to the institutions that host the canon make that costly.

stakeholders.name: monetary_statisticians
stakeholders.situation: Central-bank statisticians who built the monetary aggregates and payment-flow series through which electronic money first became visible to policy. The thinkable frame casts their categories as late-arriving bookkeeping that registered the true emergence decades late, converting pioneering measurement work into evidence of institutional slowness. Their exit runs through the same institutions whose self-accounting the frame flatters.

stakeholders.name: peripheral_deployment_pioneers
stakeholders.situation: Operators in smaller economies who launched functioning electronic purse and retail e-money systems years before metropolitan recognition, sometimes with no connection to the conceptual circuit at all. Diffusion-centered dating assigns origins to wherever the ideas were legible, so their deployments fall outside the arc entirely. With no seat in the journals, anniversaries, or central-bank histories that fix the chronology, they have no channel through which their dates could count.

stakeholders.name: economic_methodologists
stakeholders.situation: Researchers who study how economics constructs its objects, including how statistical practice creates categories such as monetary aggregates. They watch the dating contest from outside every camp, treat all three periodizations as framing choices with distributive effects, and hold no stake in which anchor prevails.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides one shared answer to 'when did electronic money begin,' anchored in the opening of technical and social possibility rather than in deployment statistics — enabling common syllabi, organized archives, commemorative calendars, and cumulative citation across history, economics, and policy institutions.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves attributional credit and narrative authority from operational implementers (clearing, card, and funds-transfer engineering communities) and from measurement institutions (monetary statisticians) toward conceptual innovators and their chroniclers; secondarily moves research funding, curricular slots, and commemorative visibility along the same gradient.
six_questions.absent_voices: Peripheral-market deployment pioneers: operators whose systems ran before, or entirely outside, the metropolitan conceptual conversation and were never assigned a thinkable moment. They would object that diffusion-centered dating presupposes a center, and that their systems' absence from the origin story reflects where ideas were legible, not when money went electronic. They are absent because the forums that fix the canon — journals, anniversary convenings, central-bank histories — draw contributors from the conceptual circuit, and because their documentation sits in local archives no canon-building project indexes.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the convention vanished overnight, textbook chronologies, commemorative calendars, funded research lines, and credit allocations would lose their anchor; the suspended priority dispute between conceptual and operational claimants would reopen immediately; and central-bank lineage storytelling would need rebuilding. The payment rails themselves would run unchanged — the rearrangement is in the record-keeping and credit economy, not in the systems.
six_questions.founding_problem: By the mid-1990s the accumulation of fragmentary electronic-payment developments — funds transfer, card networks, stored value, early digital-cash experiments — had made 'when did electronic money begin?' unanswerable by any single deployment date, while curricula, commemorations, and policy lineages needed one narratable origin. The thinkability answer dissolved the multiplicity of candidate thresholds into a single gradual arc that begins before any statistic could register it.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Corroborated from outside the benefiting parties: economic methodologists studying the construction of economic categories attest that the periodization problem is real while disputing the thinkable anchor specifically; published memoirs and oral histories of payment-systems engineers attest the attribution grievance the frame generates; central-bank historical publications attest the practical institutional demand for an origin story. No source outside the dispute attests that the thinkable anchor is the correct resolution — the corroboration covers the existence of the founding problem, not the adequacy of this reading's answer to it.
